about: Generals' perks (decision 'Next 2': family and appointed generals, great people with perks). skills: tactics (winning the day), leadership (holding men together, fewer losses), siegecraft (taking walls), logistics (marching, supply, less attrition), seamanship (fleets); each 1-10, 5 an ordinary commander. A perk adds to skills or to an effect: cavalry, infantry, elephants, missile (that arm's strength in battle), hills, forest, marsh, desert, river (fighting on that ground), pursuit (losses the beaten enemy suffers), losses (own losses: negative is fewer), veterans (experience gained), siege (siege speed). great: only great people have it. Modelled on the commanders in Polybius, Plutarch, Livy and Arrian. Our own data, free for any use. historical: the great commanders of 300 BC, who lead their realm's first army from the start (by realm key and the name of the family member): Pyrrhos (Plutarch, Pyrrhus), Demetrios Poliorketes (Diodorus 20), Seleukos and his elephants at Ipsus, Lysimachos, Ptolemaios I, Agathokles of Syracuse, who carried the war to Africa in 310 BC.

perks.name: Master of horse
perks.description: Handles cavalry as Alexander's companions were handled: the decisive charge on the wing.

perks.name: Drillmaster
perks.description: Keeps the heavy foot in order through any day.

perks.name: Leader of light troops
perks.description: Uses slingers, archers and javelinmen to wear the enemy down before the lines meet.

perks.name: Master of elephants
perks.description: Knows how to use elephants and how to keep them from turning on his own lines.

perks.name: Hill fighter
perks.description: Grew up fighting in the mountains, like the Samnites against Rome.

perks.name: Forest fighter
perks.description: At home among trees and ambushes.

perks.name: Desert raider
perks.description: Moves and fights in the dry lands as the Nabataeans did.

perks.name: River crosser
perks.description: Forces rivers as Alexander forced the Granicus and the Hydaspes.

perks.name: Cautious
perks.description: Fights only when sure: fewer losses, fewer great victories.

perks.name: Reckless
perks.description: Throws everything in at once, like Flaminius at Trasimene.

perks.name: Beloved of the men
perks.description: The soldiers would follow him anywhere.

perks.name: Harsh disciplinarian
perks.description: Feared rather than loved: steady in battle, weary on the march.

perks.name: Engineer
perks.description: Builds ramps, towers and engines, like Demetrios the Besieger.

perks.name: Quartermaster
perks.description: Keeps the army fed and shod: less sickness and desertion.

perks.name: Relentless pursuer
perks.description: Turns a won field into a rout.

perks.name: Sea captain
perks.description: Knows winds, coasts and the ram.

perks.name: Old soldier
perks.description: Has seen twenty campaigns and forgotten none of them.

perks.name: Untried
perks.description: Has never commanded in the field.

perks.name: Genius of war
perks.description: One of the great captains of the age, of the kind of Pyrrhos or Hannibal.

perks.name: Father of his soldiers
perks.description: Reforms the army he leads, as Marius and Scipio did.

perks.name: Stormer of cities
perks.description: No wall holds against him: a Poliorketes.

perks.name: Lord of the sea
perks.description: An admiral of the kind of Duilius or Hamilcar.
